title: A Simple Vision for Your AI Use
author: Paul Matthews
summary: Paul Matthews introduces 'AI for Better Basics', a framework and series arguing for a specific, focused vision of AI use in education: employing AI to do the evidence-based basics of teaching better. He situates this vision in the context of a widening learning gap, noting that the disruptions of 2021-2022 worsened already-wide achievement gaps precisely when AI arrived with the capacity to handle in seconds what previously consumed teachers' evenings, such as text differentiation, sentence stems, and resource adaptation. Matthews frames the series explicitly as not being about AI per se but about improving student literacy, promising ten evidence-based practices covered with descriptions, evidence summaries, classroom prompts, and implementation tips. The goal is to give every teacher, regardless of subject or AI skill level, the practical ability to do the basics better for their learners.
points: AI arrived before educators had a clear purpose for it, which is why a focused, evidence-grounded vision beats a general embrace of AI tools.
The strongest case for AI is not novelty but narrow uplift: using it to close the resource gap that made high-quality differentiation too time-costly for most teachers.
Tasks that once took an hour (text differentiation) or thirty minutes (sentence stems) now take seconds, changing what is possible in a planning period.
The learning gap between struggling and advanced learners is wider than ever after the 2021-2022 disruptions, creating urgent need for AI-enabled differentiated support.
Grounding AI use in evidence-based practices guards against both hype and misapplication.
quotes: Put simply, the presence of AI preceded the purpose of AI. So what should we use AI for?

We can use Artificial Intelligence to do the evidence-based basics of education better. This is a powerful vision for AI because, while AI didn't arrive with a purpose, it arrived into a specific context.
The learning gap — the distance between struggling and advanced learners — is yawning wider than ever before.
That text differentiation that took an hour? I can finish it before I finish my coffee. Those sentence stems that took half an hour? They now take seconds.
This is not primarily a series about AI. It's not about more AI, less AI, or better AI. It's a deeply human goal. It is a series about helping students improve their literacy.
